content.text: Now writing the changes. First the database schema: `leaderboard` will hold one row per player, and `scores` will hold one row per finished game.

python - <<'EOF'
p='setup.sql'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
start=s.index('-- One-time copy: players saved in the old "scores" table')
end=s.index('-- Load the 20 backup scenarios')
new='''-- Older versions used "scores" as the leaderboard itself (one row per player:
-- username, total_score, badges). If that old table is still here, copy its
-- players into "leaderboard", then rename it to scores_legacy_<timestamp> so
-- nothing is lost and "scores" can become the per-game table below.
-- Drop the legacy table yourself once you've checked the data.
DO $$
DECLARE
  legacy TEXT;
  idx    RECORD;
BEGIN
  IF to_regclass('public.scores') IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
        WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'scores' AND column_name = 'score_id') THEN
    IF (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.columns
         WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'scores'
           AND column_name IN ('username', 'total_score', 'badges')) = 3 THEN
      INSERT INTO leaderboard (username, total_score, badges)
      SELECT left(trim(username), 20), total_score, COALESCE(badges, '{}') FROM scores
       WHERE char_length(trim(username)) BETWEEN 1 AND 20
      ON CONFLICT (username) DO NOTHING;
    END IF;
    legacy := 'scores_legacy_' || to_char(clock_timestamp(), 'YYYYMMDDHH24MISS');
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE public.scores RENAME TO %I', legacy);
    -- Index names (like scores_pkey) must be unique, so rename the old ones too
    FOR idx IN SELECT i.relname FROM pg_index x JOIN pg_class i ON i.oid = x.indexrelid
                WHERE x.indrelid = format('public.%I', legacy)::regclass LOOP
      EXECUTE format('ALTER INDEX public.%I RENAME TO %I', idx.relname, legacy || '_' || idx.relname);
    END LOOP;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Old scores table renamed to %', legacy;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Table 3: scores (one row per finished game). POST /api/score writes a row
-- here and adds the points/badge to that player's leaderboard row in the same
-- transaction. run_id comes from the browser so a retried save is never
-- counted twice.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (
  score_id     BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id       TEXT UNIQUE,
  username     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES leaderboard (username) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE,
  mode         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('easy', 'medium', 'hard')),
  correct      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (correct >= 0),
  rounds       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rounds > 0),
  points       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  passed       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  badge        TEXT,                        -- the mode, if this run earned its badge
  played_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS scores_player_idx ON scores (username, played_at DESC);

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
s=s.replace('''-- Table 2: the leaderboard (one row per player). Feeds the Leaderboard and
-- PhishSense Masters cards on the home screen. Columns match what server.js
-- writes in POST /api/score and what app.js reads: username, total_score, badges.''','''-- Table 2: the leaderboard (one row per player: running total and badges).
-- Feeds the Leaderboard and PhishSense Masters cards on the home screen.''')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "Table\|scores" setup.sql | head

1	-- PhishSense database setup (Vultr Managed PostgreSQL, database "appdb")
2	-- server.js runs this file every time it starts. It is safe to run again:
3	-- tables are only created if missing and existing scenarios are never changed.
4	-- You can also run it yourself: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f setup.sql
5	
6	-- Table 1: every scenario (our 20 backups + whatever Gemini makes)
7	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenarios (
8	  scenario_id  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
9	  source       TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'sheet' (backup) or 'gemini'
10	  channel      TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'email' or 'sms'
11	  difficulty   TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
12	  sender       TEXT NOT NULL,
13	  subject      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
14	  body         TEXT NOT NULL,
15	  link         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
16	  game_answer  TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'Phish' or 'Legit'
17	  red_flags    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
18	  explanation  TEXT NOT NULL,
19	  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
20	);
21	
22	-- Table 2: the leaderboard (one row per player). Feeds the Leaderboard and
23	-- PhishSense Masters cards on the home screen. Columns match what server.js
24	-- writes in POST /api/score and what app.js reads: username, total_score, badges.
25	-- An older setup had a read-only VIEW named "leaderboard" over "scores". A view
26	-- would block this table from being created, so replace it if it's still there.
27	DO $$
28	BEGIN
29	  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
30	             WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'leaderboard' AND c.relkind IN ('v', 'm')) THEN
31	    EXECUTE (SELECT CASE relkind WHEN 'v' THEN 'DROP VIEW public.leaderboard'
32	                                 ELSE 'DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW public.leaderboard' END
33	               FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'public.leaderboard'::regclass);
34	  END IF;
35	END $$;
36	
37	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard (
38	  username     TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
39	  total_score  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
40	  badges       TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',   -- any of 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
41	  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
42	);
43	
44	-- Speeds up the two ranking queries (Leaderboard and Masters)
45	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_rank_idx
46	  ON leaderboard ((cardinality(badges)) DESC, total_score DESC);
47	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_badges_idx ON leaderboard USING GIN (badges);

-- PhishSense database setup (Vultr Managed PostgreSQL, database "appdb")
-- server.js runs this file every time it starts. It is safe to run again:
-- tables are only created if missing and existing scenarios are never changed.
-- You can also run it yourself: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f setup.sql

-- Table 1: every scenario (our 20 backups + whatever Gemini makes)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenarios (
  scenario_id  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source       TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'sheet' (backup) or 'gemini'
  channel      TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'email' or 'sms'
  difficulty   TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
  sender       TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  body         TEXT NOT NULL,
  link         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  game_answer  TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'Phish' or 'Legit'
  red_flags    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  explanation  TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Table 2: the leaderboard (one row per player). Feeds the Leaderboard and
-- PhishSense Masters cards on the home screen. Columns match what server.js
-- writes in POST /api/score and what app.js reads: username, total_score, badges.
-- An older setup had a read-only VIEW named "leaderboard" over "scores". A view
-- would block this table from being created, so replace it if it's still there.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
             WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'leaderboard' AND c.relkind IN ('v', 'm')) THEN
    EXECUTE (SELECT CASE relkind WHEN 'v' THEN 'DROP VIEW public.leaderboard'
                                 ELSE 'DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW public.leaderboard' END
               FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'public.leaderboard'::regclass);
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard (
  username     TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  total_score  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  badges       TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',   -- any of 'easy', 'medium', 'hard'
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Speeds up the two ranking queries (Leaderboard and Masters)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_rank_idx
  ON leaderboard ((cardinality(badges)) DESC, total_score DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS leaderboard_badges_idx ON leaderboard USING GIN (badges);

    INSERT INTO leaderboard (username, total_score, badges, updated_at)
    SELECT left(username, 20), total_score, badges, updated_at FROM scores
    WHERE char_length(username) BETWEEN 1 AND 20
    ON CONFLICT (username) DO NOTHING;
  END IF;
END $$;

content.text:
Finished games are now saved to your database, and you can look them up after a game ends. The Leaderboard and the PhishSense Masters list both pull every player from the DB and fall back to scores saved in the browser when the DB is down. I tested it against a throwaway in-memory Postgres, not your real Vultr database (there's no `.env` here), so check `/api/health` after you deploy. Nothing is committed yet.

**How the two tables are used now**
- **`leaderboard`**: one row per player, with their total points and badges.
- **`scores`**: one row for every finished game (mode, number correct, points, passed, badge, time played).
- One save does both in a single transaction: it adds the game to `scores` and updates that player's `leaderboard` row. Each game carries a unique ID, so if a save is retried it is never counted twice.
- The server works out points and badges from the mode and the number correct, so the browser can't send a made-up score.

**What happens to your current `scores` table:** In PR #2, `scores` held one row per player. If your current `scores` table is still in that format, the server copies its players into `leaderboard` on startup and renames the old table to `scores_legacy_<timestamp>`, then creates the new per-game `scores` table. Nothing is deleted; drop the legacy table once you've checked the data. If your `scores` table has a different layout I don't know about, look at it before deploying.

**Getting the data back after a game** (new and updated routes in `server.js`)
- `POST /api/score` now sends back the player's totals plus the game it just saved.
- `GET /api/players/:username` gives one player's totals and their recent games.
- `GET /api/scores` gives recent games from everyone, and takes `?username=` to show one player.
- `GET /api/leaderboard` now returns every player (it used to stop at 50), with games played, best game and last played. `GET /api/masters` returns every player with all three badges.

**Fallback to local** (`public/app.js`)
- Every finished game is also saved in the browser. If the DB can't be reached, the game waits in a queue and is sent automatically the next time the page loads or another game is saved.
- If the DB is down, the Leaderboard and Masters lists show the last list the DB sent plus the games saved in that browser, with a short note under each. They no longer show "Couldn't load scores".
- Opening the game as a file (practice mode) works the same as before.

**What I tested**
- On a copy of the old PR #2 `scores` table, the migration moved the players into `leaderboard`, and running setup a second time was safe.
- Saving, retrying the same game, a player name with extra spaces, bad input, and all the new routes worked.
- In the browser code with simulated DB outages: games saved while the DB was down, the fallback lists were right, and the queued games synced once with no duplicates when the DB came back.
